categories.main_business_segments: NextEra Energy, Inc. (NEE) operates two principal business segments: Florida Power & Light Company (FPL), a rate-regulated electric utility serving over six million customer accounts in Florida, and NextEra Energy Resources (NEER), which includes competitive energy and rate-regulated transmission businesses and is the world’s largest generator of renewable energy from wind and solar, as well as a leader in battery storage.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FPL’s operations are based on a diverse generation portfolio including natural gas, solar, nuclear, and battery storage, with significant investments in transmission and distribution infrastructure. NEER develops, constructs, and operates wind, solar, nuclear, and battery storage facilities, leveraging advanced renewable technologies, long-term power purchase agreements, and innovative grid-scale storage solutions. Both segments utilize sophisticated energy trading and risk management systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: FPL primarily serves residential, commercial, and industrial retail electricity customers in Florida, with a small portion of revenue from wholesale customers. NEER’s customers include utilities, retail electricity providers, power cooperatives, municipal electric providers, and commercial and industrial clients across the U.S. and Canada, primarily through long-term contracts for renewable energy, capacity, and related products.
categories.geographic_coverage: FPL operates throughout most of the east and lower west coasts of Florida and parts of northwest Florida. NEER owns and operates generation and transmission assets in 41 U.S. states and four Canadian provinces, with a strong presence in Texas, the Midwest, the West, and the South, as well as select international investments.
categories.supply_chain_position: FPL operates as a vertically integrated, downstream utility, managing generation, transmission, and distribution to end customers. NEER is positioned as an independent power producer (IPP) and transmission owner, primarily downstream in the supply chain, but also participates in midstream activities through natural gas pipelines and storage, as well as energy marketing and trading.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: NEE’s strategic focus is on expanding clean energy leadership, investing in renewable generation, battery storage, and grid modernization, while maintaining low customer bills and high reliability. The company emphasizes innovation in large-scale renewables, storage, and transmission, and actively pursues growth through new project development, technology deployment, and selective acquisitions. R&D efforts target cost reductions, operational efficiency, and integration of renewables with storage.
categories.revenue_model: FPL generates revenue primarily through regulated retail electricity sales, with rates set by the Florida Public Service Commission, and additional revenue from cost recovery clauses and limited wholesale transactions. NEER’s revenue model is based on long-term contracted sales of energy, capacity, renewable energy credits, and ancillary services, as well as energy marketing, trading, and, to a lesser extent, merchant sales into spot markets.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FPL faces limited direct competition due to its regulated monopoly status but competes with self-generation and alternative energy providers. NEER competes with other independent power producers and utilities in the wholesale market, such as NextEra’s peers in renewables (e.g., Invenergy, EDF Renewables, Pattern Energy, Orsted, and utilities with renewable portfolios). NEE is recognized as a market leader in renewables, with scale, execution, and creditworthiness as key differentiators.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: NEE is one of the largest electric power and energy infrastructure companies in North America, with total assets of $190 billion and 2024 operating revenues of $24.8 billion. Net income attributable to NEE was $6.95 billion in 2024. The company has demonstrated sustained profitable growth, driven by ongoing capital investment in renewables, storage, and regulated utility infrastructure, and maintains a strong investment-grade credit profile.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: NEE’s value proposition centers on delivering reliable, low-cost, and clean energy to customers, with FPL emphasizing industry-leading reliability, customer service, and low bills. NEER differentiates itself as the world’s largest producer of wind and solar energy, offering customers long-term, cost-effective, and sustainable energy solutions, backed by a track record of project execution, innovation, and financial strength.
